primary_claim: Non-adversarial proposer-critic debate improves a weak judge's macro-F1 over consultancy on code, logic, and math tasks (5 of 8 tested strong-debater/weak-judge pairings), but only when the judge is above a capability threshold where it can act as a verifier rather than a summarizer of critic reasoning; debate's gains concentrate in reducing false-positive endorsement of wrong proposer answers rather than improving recall of correct answers, and rebuttal turns add no measurable benefit over opening-only debate.

effect.metric: judge macro-F1 across debate/consultancy formats; judge recall conditional on critic correctness
effect.value: debate improves macro-F1 over consultancy on 5/8 pairings (no effect on the other 2, weakest debater-judge pairs); e.g. Gemini 3.1 Pro/3 Flash logic: full debate 0.906 vs full consultancy 0.766; Opus 4.6/4.5 logic: 0.773 vs 0.615; opening-only debate performs comparably to full debate with rebuttals in nearly all rows

contradicts_or_qualifies: the assumption that rebuttal turns are necessary for debate to work; the paper finds opening-only debate performs indistinguishably from full debate with rebuttals
datasets abandoned for saturation (ZebraLogic, ARC AGI, Knights and Knaves, HumanEval+) or poor machine-generated label quality (BigCodeBench, APPS, OMNI-Math)
stated_future_work: test debate on fuzzier tasks (e.g. experiment design, research steering) that lack easily scorable final answers, as proxies for automation of AI research
study training-time dynamics and reward allocation under different debate protocols, especially with longer RL runs that give debaters more latitude to exploit the protocol
engineer failures in these protocols to test the theory debate is built on
limitations_stated: results are restricted to programmatically verifiable domains (math, code, logic) with easily scorable final answers; unclear whether they transfer to fuzzier tasks
judge and critic are always from the same model family in these experiments, so their failure modes may be correlated in ways a cross-family judge would not be susceptible to
inter-row comparisons of judge recall when critic is wrong are likely invalid due to a selection effect: stronger critics get fewer, likely-harder questions wrong
results are for non-adversarial, inference-time reward allocation, not train-time reward allocation under optimization pressure
some considered datasets were abandoned due to poor machine-generated accuracy label quality or model saturation
quote: We find that debate helps macro-F1 on five of eight pairings and has no effect on the other two. It helps all but the weakest debater-judge pairings... These gains mostly concentrate in helping judges reject wrong proposers.
